facts.statement: The type specimen, a partial skeleton designated FPDM-V97122, was discovered in the Kitadani quarry near Katsuyama in Fukui Prefecture.
facts.quote: The type specimen is a partial skeleton (designated FPDM-V97122) discovered in the Kitadani quarry near Katsuyama in the Fukui prefecture.

facts.statement: Numerous humeri, femurs, and teeth from other individuals have been found in the same quarry and assigned to Fukuiraptor.
facts.quote: The remains of many other individuals have been found in the quarry, with numerous humeri, femurs, and teeth being assigned to this species.

facts.statement: A tooth designated NDC-P0001 found in the Sebayashi Formation has been referred to Fukuiraptor.
facts.quote: A tooth (NDC-P0001) discovered in a block of conglomerate from the Sebayashi Formation has been referred to Fukuiraptor as well.

facts.statement: Fukuiraptor is considered either one of the earliest members of Megaraptora or a close relative of Australovenator.
facts.quote: Fukuiraptor may have been one of the basalmost members of Megaraptora, or a sister taxon to Australovenator.

facts.statement: Fukuiraptor was a relatively lightly built animal, indicated by its slender phalanges.
facts.quote: As indicated by its slender phalanges, Fukuiraptor was a relatively lightly built animal, regardless of its maturity.

facts.statement: The immature holotype was initially estimated to be 4.2 meters long and weigh 175 kilograms.
facts.quote: The immature holotype is estimated to reach 4.2 m long and weigh 175 kg in its initial description.

facts.statement: In 2010, Gregory Paul estimated Fukuiraptor to be 5 meters long and weigh 300 kilograms.
facts.quote: In 2010 Gregory Paul gave a length of 5 meters (16 ft) and a weight of 300 kg (660 lbs).

facts.statement: In 2014, Fukuiraptor's body mass was estimated to be up to 250 kilograms.
facts.quote: In 2014, its body mass was estimated up to 250 kg.

facts.statement: In 2016, Molina-Pérez and Larramendi estimated Fukuiraptor to be 4.3 meters long and weigh 590 kilograms.
facts.quote: Molina-Pérez and Larramendi estimated a length of 4.3 meters (14.1 ft) and a weight of 590 kg (1,300 lbs) in 2016.

facts.statement: Fukuiraptor's teeth resemble carcharodontosaurids in being compressed, blade-like, and having wrinkled enamel, and tyrannosaurids in having oblique blood grooves near serrations.
facts.quote: The distinctive teeth of Fukuiraptor show similarities with both carcharodontosaurids (being very compressed and blade-like, as well as having wrinkled enamel) and tyrannosaurids (having oblique blood grooves near the serrations).

facts.statement: The holotype possessed very large, flat hand claws that were initially mistaken for foot claws, leading to its early classification as a dromaeosaurid.
facts.quote: The holotype also had very large and flat manual unguals (hand claws), which played a role in its initial classification as a dromaeosaurid (as the hand claws were mistaken for foot claws) as well as its current classification as a megaraptoran.

facts.statement: Fukuiraptor was initially classified as a dromaeosaurid and considered a carnosaur related to Allosaurus.
facts.quote: Initially considered a member of the Dromaeosauridae when first discovered, its initial describers considered it a carnosaur, related to Allosaurus.

facts.statement: Recent studies classify Fukuiraptor as a megaraptoran, potentially part of the family Neovenatoridae.
facts.quote: More recent studies place it as a megaraptoran, an enigmatic group which may have been part of the family Neovenatoridae.

facts.statement: Fukuiraptor lived from the Hauterivian to the Aptian, between 132.6 and 113.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Hauterivian to Aptian (132.6 to 113.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Researchers believe the type specimen was immature and that adults of Fukuiraptor may have been larger.
facts.quote: It is thought that this specimen was not mature and an adult may have been larger.

facts.statement: Most other individuals found at the locality were juveniles, with the smallest being less than a quarter the size of the holotype.
facts.quote: However, the other individuals recovered from the same locality are mostly juveniles that were smaller than the holotype (Azuma & Currie, 2006), in the smallest case less than a quarter of the holotype's size.
